quests.essayTopic: Revise a full introduction-to-body sequence explaining why a city's new pothole reporting app improved road maintenance response times
options: Most delays traced back to reports arriving through inconsistent channels, phone calls, emails, and in-person visits, that were never centrally tracked.
Average repair response time dropped to under two weeks, and repeat reports for the same pothole dropped by nearly ninety percent, a genuinely separate benefit from speed alone.
The city introduced a single reporting app that logged every report with a location, photo, and automatic status update visible to the resident who filed it.
Residents previously waited an average of six weeks for a reported pothole to be repaired, often reporting the same pothole multiple times without any visible response.
quests.hint: This capstone repair should combine everything from this file: specific context replacing a vague opening, a clearly identified problem before its solution, and a supporting detail that avoids repeating the same point about speed.
quests.explanation: The specific context replaces a vague opening with a concrete, measured fact. The problem identified names the specific cause, scattered reporting channels, before the solution correctly follows it. The distinct supporting detail adds a genuinely separate benefit, reduced repeat reports, rather than repeating the speed point already made.
quests.thesisStatement: A centralized pothole reporting app improved response times and, separately, sharply reduced repeat reports for the same issue.

quests.essayTopic: Revise a full body-to-conclusion sequence explaining why a library's new self-checkout kiosks reduced checkout wait times
options: The kiosks were sourced from a supplier also used by several nearby libraries, though what matters here is that the shared supplier meant staff could be trained using materials other libraries had already tested and refined.
Checkout wait times had grown noticeably as the library added more forms of media, each requiring different manual processing steps at the counter.
Self-checkout kiosks let visitors scan and check out most items themselves, removing the bottleneck of a single staffed counter processing every different format.
Removing a bottleneck, it turns out, did more for wait times than simply adding a second staffed counter ever could have.
quests.hint: This capstone repair should combine everything from this file: a clear problem-cause connection, a solution that directly answers it, a supporting detail reframed to stay relevant, and a genuine closing insight rather than a flat repetition.
quests.explanation: The problem and cause together establish exactly what was going wrong and why. The solution directly answers that specific cause, and the reframed relevant detail avoids becoming an irrelevant tangent about the supplier by tying back to training efficiency. The genuine insight closes with a memorable reframing rather than a flat repetition.
quests.thesisStatement: Self-checkout kiosks reduced library wait times by removing the single-counter bottleneck that had grown alongside the collection.
